title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred from context): 𝓜 is a category of graded modules over a graded ring A concentrated in degrees ≥ 0. This is plausibly the module theory over a graded-commutative dg-algebra with divided powers that the next page sets up. For an integer N, 𝓜_N is the full subcategory of modules M with M_i = 0 for i < N. For N ≤ N', i_{N,N'}: 𝓜_{N'} → 𝓜_N is the inclusion.

(1) Right adjoint. τ_{N',N}(M) ⊂ M is the largest submodule concentrated in degrees ≥ N', namely M_{≥N'} = ⊕_{i≥N'} M_i. This is a submodule because A has degrees ≥ 0. The page writes Hom_{𝓜_N}(i(P), M) ≅ Hom_{𝓜_{N'}}(P, τ(M)), and both sides are just Hom_𝓜 since the subcategories are full.

(2) Left adjoint. q_{N',N}(M) = M / (submodule generated by the M_i, i < N'). Any map M → P with P ∈ 𝓜_{N'} kills the M_i for i < N', hence kills the submodule they generate. This gives Hom_{𝓜_N}(M, i(P)) = Hom_𝓜(q(M), P). The two-row picture (0 0 M_N … M_{N'-1} M_{N'} … over 0 0 0 … 0 P_{N'} P_{N'+1} …) illustrates the degrees.

(3) Remarks in the NB.
- q and τ are 'localization functors', i.e. adjoints of a fully faithful functor.
- q commutes with all colimits, hence is right exact. It is presumably not left exact, so Grothendieck does not expect a further left adjoint.
- τ is computed degreewise, so it commutes with both limits and colimits and is exact. One therefore expects τ to have a right adjoint.

In modern terms: i ⊣ τ ⊣ R with i and R fully faithful. Here τ is the Serre quotient of 𝓜_N by the Serre subcategory of modules concentrated in degrees [N, N'−1]. Together with q ⊣ i, this is a recollement-type configuration (j_! = i, j^* = τ, j_* = R). These are the abelian-level truncation functors he needs for the divided-power de Rham complex.

Purpose: bookkeeping of degree truncations, akin to the stupid filtration, for modules over a graded or dg algebra in the 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power de Rham complex.
errors: The claim that q is not left exact is correct but only asserted ('sans doute'). Example: A = k[t] with deg t = 1, N = 0, N' = 1. The inclusion tA ⊂ A maps under q to tA → A/A = 0, which is not injective.

The right adjoint of τ is only expected, not constructed. It exists by the adjoint functor theorem, since these are Grothendieck abelian categories and τ preserves colimits. Explicitly it is a coinduction-type object, R(P) = Hom_A(A_{≥N'-•}-type construction); this was not worked out on the page.
Implicit assumption: A is concentrated in degrees ≥ 0, so that M_{≥N'} is a submodule.

ideas.what: Inclusion of degree-≥N' graded modules has a right adjoint (truncation M_{≥N'}) and a left adjoint (quotient by submodule generated by low degrees)
ideas.modern_name: Truncation functors / reflective and coreflective subcategory; Serre quotient
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard homological algebra (Gabriel 1962 for Serre quotients and localization)
ideas.where_published: Not specifically; general adjunction and localization language appears in SGA 4 and Tôhoku

ideas.what: Observation that τ commutes with limits and colimits, hence should have a right adjoint, giving i ⊣ τ ⊣ R
ideas.modern_name: Recollement of abelian categories (j_! ⊣ j^* ⊣ j_*)
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 discusses open/closed gluing of topoi, the formal analogue

deep.surprise_reason: Routine adjoint-functor bookkeeping for degree truncations of graded modules; correct and standard, with no new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: 'foncteurs de localisation (car adjoint d'un foncteur pl. fidèle)' – the word is likely 'car', not part of a parenthetical 'adjoint'.

'et q_{N',N} est exact à droite (en fait, commute aux lim→ quelc.) mais en général pas à gauche sans doute – on ne s'attend pas qu'il ait encore un adj. à g.' The line 'q_{N',N}, i_{N,N'}, τ_{N',N}' is a separate marginal list of the three functors, not part of the sentence.
End: 'Par contre τ_{N',N} commute aux lim← et aux lim→ (a fortiori il est exact). Donc on s'attend à lui trouver un foncteur adjoint à droite.'
Second Hom line: 'Hom_𝓜(M/ss-module engendré par les M_i, i<N', P)', with the subscript reading 'Hom_𝓜' (the big category).
